course_name_original: Introdução aos Circuitos e Sistemas Electrónicos (ICSE112)
course_name_en: Introduction to Electronic Circuits and Systems
syllabus_topics: Introduction to electronic systems: signal representation; types of systems (linear, non-linear, open-loop, closed-loop).
DC circuits: electric current; voltage; resistance and Ohm's law; power, energy; voltage and current sources; capacitors and inductors; Kirchhoff's Laws.
AC circuits: reactance, phasors and complex numbers; series and parallel circuits.
Amplification and feedback: gain, frequency response, input and output impedance; operational amplifiers – characteristics, parameters, circuits.
Electronic devices: diodes, bipolar transistors and MOSFETs.
Digital electronics: logic levels and noise margins, propagation delay, rise and fall times, fan-out and fan-in, power consumption; TTL and CMOS families.
Power supplies: batteries; unregulated and regulated sources; switched-mode power supplies; specifications.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory work (6 assignments L1 to L6)

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade is calculated as 40% of the laboratory grade + 30% of MAP45 + 30% of the normal season exam (E-EN). A minimum grade of 8.0 is required for MAP45 and E-EN, and 9.5 for the laboratory grade. In the resit period, it's possible to repeat the 1st MAP45 or the exam (2nd MAP45), maintaining the normal season formula. Alternatively, for all material, the final grade is 40% of the laboratory grade + 60% of the resit exam (E-ER). Student-workers can choose between normal or resit period rules. For the special period, the final grade is 100% based on the exam.
bibliography: Neil Storey, Electrical & Electronic Systems, Prentice Hall, 2004 (main)
David Crecraft, Stephen Gergely, Analog Electronics: Circuits, Systems and Signal Processing, Elsevier, 2002 (main)
Sedra & Smith, Microelectronic Circuits, 5th edition, Saunders College Publishing, 2004 (main)
institution: Universidade De Lisboa — LERC Eng. de Telecomunicações e Informática (IST)
degree: Licenciatura em Engenharia de Telecomunicações e Informática (LERC)
